title: Synthetic latency profile generator and dashboard spec
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This document defines the Synthetic Latency Profile Generator (SLPG) and the associated dashboard panel and alert mapping required to validate alerting sensitivity, SLO coverage, and operator workflows for latency-related degradations across multi-tenant LLM inference workloads. The SLPG is a lightweight service used by platform teams and SREs to craft reproducible latency distributions (profiles) and exercise dashboards, alert rules, and runbooks without touching production traffic.

Motivation
----------
- Latency regressions at token or request granularity are often subtle and can evade production detection until customer impact is visible.
- Operator dashboards and synthetic labs need realistic, configurable latency shapes to validate detection thresholds and escalation paths.
- The SLPG provides a single, auditable source of synthetic profiles so dashboards, alerting, and runbooks remain aligned with realistic failure modes.

Scope
-----
- Includes the SLPG configuration spec, sample profiles, dashboard panel mapping, alerting thresholds, and the operator triage runbook for synthetic latency incidents.
- Covers region-aware and model-variant-aware profiles.
- Excludes generation of synthetic model outputs or billing metrics; token-cost and billing signals are out of scope for the SLPG and are covered by separate chargeback tests.

Definitions
-----------
- Synthetic profile: a parametric distribution of observed request latencies injected into the telemetry pipeline labelled as synthetic.test=true.
- Tail latency window: P95/P99 computed over a sliding 5-minute window unless otherwise noted.
- Heatset: a set of tenants or model variants used when simulating hot-path degradations.

Architecture overview
---------------------
1. SLPG service (k8s) hosts a profile API and a scheduler.
2. Profiles are emitted as telemetry events to the ingestion endpoint and flagged with synthetic.test=true and profile_id.
3. Telemetry processors apply the same aggregation rules as production (tokenization grouping, tenant labels, region, model_variant).
4. Dashboards consume derived metrics from the normal telemetry store; panels include a synthetic toggle to overlay synthetic profiles.

Data sources and transformation rules
------------------------------------
- Input: profile JSON -> scheduler -> ingestion (HTTP) -> metrics pipeline.
- All synthetic events must include: profile_id, scenario_name, heatset_id (optional), model_variant (optional), region.
- Timestamps must be monotonic; profile playback can accelerate time for lab runs.
- Synthetic events are tagged with customer_id=synthetic and tenant_id reserved synthetic_* to avoid billing confusion.

Sample profile JSON
-------------------
(Example to paste into SLPG API)

{
  \"profile_id\": \"p99-delta-2026-01\",
  \"scenario_name\": \"p99-step-up\",
  \"duration_seconds\": 900,
  \"rps\": 10,
  \"shape\": [
    { \"t\": 0, \"p50\": 30, \"p95\": 60, \"p99\": 120 },
    { \"t\": 300, \"p50\": 30, \"p95\": 400, \"p99\": 1200 },
    { \"t\": 600, \"p50\": 28, \"p95\": 70, \"p99\": 150 }
  ],
  \"heatset_id\": \"web-search-ht1\",
  \"regions\": [\"us-west-2\", \"eu-west-1\"]
}

Dashboard panel mapping (required panels)
----------------------------------------
Use these panels in the operator \"Latency Playground\" dashboard. For each panel include the metric query, the visual type, and the synthetic overlay toggle.

| Panel name | Metric query (example) | Visual | Purpose |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Synthetic P99 Timeline | rate(latency_p99{job=\\\"telemetry-agg\\\", synthetic.test!~\\\"|false\\\"}) by (region,model_variant) | line + shaded band | Validate P99 slope and detect step increases |
| Latency distribution heatmap | histogram(latency_ms) filter synthetic | heatmap | Visualize distribution shift and hotspot models |
| Synthetic vs Production delta | delta(latency_p99{synthetic.test=true}, latency_p99{synthetic.test=false}) | bar | Quantify detection margin |
| Operator SLO coverage | sum(slo_violations{synthetic.test=true}) / sum(requests{synthetic.test=true}) | gauge + threshold | Verify synthetic scenario breaches SLO as expected |

Alerting thresholds and rationale
--------------------------------
Alert rules should reference the synthetic playback label during lab runs but remain disabled for normal production. For canary validation, enable on demand and require manual acknowledge before auto-escalation.

- Alert: Synthetic P99 step-up (pager)
  - Condition: increase of production P99 by >= 3x sustained for 2 consecutive 5m windows and synthetic_playback.label=enabled
  - Severity: P1 (during lab); otherwise suppressed
  - Justification: catches large step regressions introduced by kernel/allocator changes

- Alert: Synthetic tiny drift (email)
  - Condition: production P99 delta >= 15ms but < 3x for 10m
  - Severity: P3
  - Justification: noise -> operator review 

Operator triage runbook (synthetic-latency-positive)
---------------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge the synthetic test run in the orchestration UI (who initiated it?).
2. Confirm profile_id and regions. Use SLPG UI or API: curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://slpg.internal/api/v1/profiles/<profile_id>
3. Verify synthetic.test=true label is present on telemetry (query in Metrics UI).
4. If the test was expected:
   - If SLOs are breached, record test outcome and close the loop with release/QA team.
   - If alerting thresholds triggered unexpectedly, run the sensitivity review (see section below).
5. If the test was NOT expected:
   - Immediately stop playback: POST /slpg/api/v1/stop/<profile_id>
   - Escalate to platform-oncall and mark incident as synthetic-misfire.

Sensitivity review checklist (when alerts misfire)
--------------------------------------------------
- Confirm that metric aggregation windows match dashboard expectations (5m sliding vs fixed bucket).
- Check telemetry label parity: synthetic.test, profile_id, heatset_id, model_variant.
- Re-run the profile with smaller amplitude: halve p95/p99 values; observe alert delta.
- Validate that synthetic events do not route to billing pipelines.
- If noise persists, add a temporary override tag synthetic.tolerance=high and repeat.

Rollout and governance
----------------------
- Phase 1 (Q4 2025): internal lab-only rollout; SLPG behind feature flag.
- Phase 2 (Q1 2026): operator-accessible catalog of vetted scenarios.
- Phase 3 (Q2 2026): integration with canary pipelines for compiler/runtime rollouts.

Ownership and contacts
----------------------
- Primary owner: eng-platform - observability subgroup (Avery Chen).
- Secondary: eng-sre oncall rotation for test-day monitoring (Diego Morales).
- Tooling: infra-telemetry (instrumentation) is responsible for the ingestion adapters.

Testing and validation matrix
----------------------------
- Unit test: profile parser, 100% coverage for validation errors.
- Integration test: throughput and label propagation to metrics store.
- Lab test: run canonical profiles (p50-noise, p99-step-up, tail-saturation) and verify dashboard overlays and alert triggers.

Compatibility and safety notes
------------------------------
- Synthetic events are excluded from billing and SLA reporting via tenant_id=synthetic_* and a pipeline filter.
- Avoid using real customer tenant IDs when authoring heatsets.
- SLPG must authenticate with a scoped service account; playback tokens expire after 24h.

Change log
----------
- 2025-11-10: Document created, initial draft of profile schema and dashboard mapping.
- 2025-12-15: Added operator triage runbook and sample profile.
- 2026-01-20: Finalized rollout phases and security notes.

Appendix: Quick CLI snippets
---------------------------
Create a profile:
curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d @p99-step-up.json https://slpg.internal/api/v1/profiles

Start playback:
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://slpg.internal/api/v1/playback/start/<profile_id>?regions=us-west-2,eu-west-1

Stop playback:
curl -X POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://slpg.internal/api/v1/playback/stop/<profile_id>
